Pre-2026 sr/hr human translations used 'protok/protoka' — consistent with current glossary entries (confirmed match). bg RESOLVED (Tom, 2026-07-13): native engineer's 2026-07-06 clarification confirmed both 'дебит' (colloquial/general register) and 'водно количество' (academic/hydraulic-engineering register, used at university for Q) are acceptable. lpn.context: Flow velocity (speed of water). Appears in all calculators.
lpn.translation_notes: Most languages use a direct cognate of 'velocity'. Do not use a word meaning 'speed' in a general sense if a more precise hydraulic term exists. lpn.context: Dimensionless ratio of vertical drop to horizontal distance (rise/run). Used as channel slope (S_0) and friction slope in Manning and Darcy-Weisbach calculators. English aliases 'slope' and 'grade' (u_grade/u_gradePercent) both point here.
lpn.translation_notes: WMO No. 385 entry 477 ('energy gradient') confirms Russian: 'энергетический уклон' (energy slope) — the base term 'уклон' is WMO-verified. In open-channel hydraulics, 'slope' is the energy gradient — not a geometric angle. Use the civil engineering term for gradient/grade, not a geographic or topographic term. rc.context: Angular rock placed to resist erosion on channel beds and banks. Appears in Manning Trapezoidal Channel and Rock Chute calculators.
rc.translation_notes: No direct single-word equivalent in most languages. Use the established local engineering term — this varies significantly by country. In Spanish, 'enrocado' (general) or 'escollera' (bank protection) are both used; lead with 'enrocado'. Bulgarian terms verified/corrected by a native Bulgarian engineer, 2026-07 (dev/Bulgarian-engineer-feedback.md). bg: 'каменна облицовка' (stone lining), not 'каменна наброска'. 2026-07-13 reconciliation pass (roadmap item 42): glossary updated to match incumbent, internally-consistent lang-file usage discovered by 5 independent category-5-wave-1 translation agents (it, pt, ru, tr) — glossary values were stale, not the shipped files. Task 97 (2026-07-13): tr's rock-chute (rc_) translation agent had actually diverged from this glossary value, using 'parça taşı' (rock fragment/piece) in 4 places instead of 'taş dolgu'; no native Turkish reviewer was available, so resolved by an AI (Opus) judgment call reasoning from suite convention — 'taş dolgu' ('stone fill', the established DSİ/TS term, cf. 'taş dolgu baraj' = rockfill dam) is correct for both the bulk-material and D50 particle-sizing senses, matching how es/fr/pt/ru all keep one bulk-material word rather than switching to a fragment/particle term for sizing contexts. Lang file corrected to 'taş dolgu' throughout; treat as our best-effort resolution, not pending native review (see CLAUDE.md 'Native review is real only when feedback actually lands'). Task 98 riprap audit (2026-07-13): found 6 of 26 languages (am, bn, he, hi, id, ur) had phonetically TRANSLITERATED the English word 'riprap' as a borrowed loanword instead of translating the concept — a real translation-quality defect, not a stylistic choice, concentrated in this specific bare/short-label term. English source renamed 'riprap' → 'rock lining' (see CLAUDE.md 'Write English source strings in Simple English') specifically because a transparent two-word English compound is much less likely to be transliterated than an opaque-looking jargon word; all 6 languages' rc_/mtc_ occurrences were corrected to real native terms in the same pass (each reusing that language's own already-successful translation pattern found elsewhere in its file). zh was separately found to use three inconsistent terms (块石/护坡/抛石) for this concept across different rc_ keys — not a transliteration issue, but the same 'pick one term and use it everywhere' defect — resolved by standardizing on 护坡 (slope protection/lining), which best matches the 'lining' sense and was already the plurality incumbent. The other 19 languages already had good native terms and needed no change — the concept translated fine, only the English word choice invited transliteration risk in weaker-resourced languages. Task 109 stage 2 (2026-07-19): ar/km/my/sw confirmed on real translated words — the phonetic-transliteration failure class (same as the 2026-07-13 rc_ audit) was checked and corrected where present.

rc.context: A steep rock-lined drop structure (also called a 'rock ramp') that conveys water rapidly down a slope in irrigation, drainage, or watershed management. Key concepts for translation: rock-lined, steep gradient, spillway or drop structure — translate the concept, not the English word 'chute'. The rock riprap matrix dissipates energy and resists erosion. Appears in Rock Chute Design (Robinson) and Robinson Rock Chute calculators.
rc.translation_notes: CRITICAL: 'Robinson' is the surname of K.M. Robinson, co-author of Robinson, Rice & Kadavy (1998) — it is a proper noun and must NEVER be translated or modified in any language. Translate only 'Rock Chute'. Concept to translate: 'rock-lined steep channel' or 'rock-lined spillway' — the drop/descent nature must be conveyed; a generic 'rock channel' is insufficient. CRITICAL for French: WMO No. 385 entry 517 establishes that the French word 'chute' means 'fall' (elevation difference) — it cannot name this structure. Use 'coursier en enrochement' (coursier = steep channel structure; enrochement = riprap). Spanish: USDA uses 'bajante de rocado' — 'bajante' (from bajar = to descend) correctly conveys the drop-structure nature; 'de rocado' = rock-lined. Russian: 'каменный быстроток' ('быстроток' = fast-flow/steep channel). Portuguese: changed from 'calha' (generic trough) to 'rampa em enrocamento' (rampa = ramp/slope, enrocamento = riprap) to convey steep character. Serbian: changed from 'жлеб' (gutter/trough) to 'брзоток' (fast-flow structure), consistent with ru/uk pattern. Bengali: changed from borrowed 'চ্যুট' (conveys nothing) to 'পাথর-আবৃত খাড়া নালা' (rock-lined steep channel). Persian: changed from generic 'آبراه سنگی' (stone waterway) to 'آبراه تند سنگچین' (تند = steep/swift, سنگچین = stone-laid/riprap). Pashto: added 'تند' (steep/swift) to original. Khmer: changed 'ចំហ' (open) to 'ជម្រាល' (sloped/inclined). NEEDS HUMAN REVIEW: am (ምቀጫ meaning uncertain), my (ထောင် may not clearly convey steep to all readers), de (Steinschütte is standard engineering term but doesn't explicitly say 'steep channel'). Turkish: changed to 'taş düşü' — 'düşü' is the established Turkish hydraulics term for a drop/chute structure (2026-07 audit; previous 'taş eğimli kanal' was descriptive but nonstandard). Spanish: NEEDS HUMAN VERIFICATION — 'bajante de rocado' claims a USDA source but 'rocado' is not standard Spanish ('enrocado' is); verify the USDA document or switch to 'bajante de enrocado'. 2026-07 reconciliation: fr/ro/ru/uk lang files updated to match this entry. NOT reconciled pending human review of the GLOSSARY side: hr 'kameni skluz' (consider 'kameni brzotok', parallel to sr/ru), bg 'каменна бързина' (consider 'каменен бързоток'), de 'Steinschütte' vs shipped 'Steingerinne' (both defensible - pick one). RESOLVED bg: native Bulgarian engineer confirmed 'каменен бързоток' (2026-07); lang file updated. Task 98 (2026-07-13): English source renamed 'Rock Chute' → 'Steep Channel' throughout the rc_ prefix (see CLAUDE.md 'Write English source strings in Simple English') — 'chute' itself is jargon-shaped English that some languages transliterated rather than translated. The earlier Bengali fix noted above only reached the calculator's title-level strings (rc_main_menu/rc_main_desc); a full-file grep found 'চ্যুট' still transliterated in 7 more rc_ body keys (rc_S0, rc_qt, rc_n_chute, rc_pond_ok_tip, rc_pond_warn_tip, rc_notes_2_def, rc_notes_3_def, rc_notes_7_def) — fixed 2026-07-13 to match the title's 'খাড়া নালা'. Hindi and Urdu had the same bare-transliteration defect suite-wide ('चूट'/'چوٹ') despite their titles being fine in some cases — fixed to 'तीव्र ढाल चैनल' (hi) and 'کھڑی نالی' (ur), applied consistently across every rc_ occurrence. Lesson: a healthy title-level translation does not guarantee the same concept was translated (vs. transliterated) in every short body label — check the whole file, not just the title strings, when auditing a jargon term.

rc.context: A steep open channel or drop structure for conveying water rapidly down a slope. Distinct from a gentle-slope irrigation canal. Per ec_lang_intent guidance: translate as 'steep channel' or 'spillway' — not as the word 'chute' borrowed into another language. Appears in Rock Chute Design (Robinson), Manning Trapezoidal Channel, and related drop-structure calculators.
rc.translation_notes: CRITICAL for French: WMO No. 385 entry 517 defines the English word 'fall' (elevation difference) as French 'chute', Spanish 'caída', and Russian 'падение'. The same pattern holds in all three WMO languages: the word for 'fall' (elevation difference) is NOT available for this hydraulic structure. 'Coursier' is the correct French term for the structure. Spanish: 'canal rápido'. Russian: 'быстроток' (the steep channel structure — distinct from 'падение' which means elevation fall). Chinese: '陡槽'. | [2026-07-20] Stage-6 sr audit found the glossary's own value (брзотек) was the stem-drift error; corrected to брзоток, consistent with ru/uk pattern and rc_ identity strings. | [2026-07-20] Stage-6 ps audit aligned to the file's own established identity-string term (تند اوبو لار) over a divergent glossary spelling, for cross-key consistency within category 5.

rc.context: Flow rate per unit width of channel (Q/B), in m²/s or ft²/s. The primary design input for the Robinson rock chute method. Appears in Rock Chute Design calculator.
rc.translation_notes: Use the hydraulic engineering term. 'Unit' here means 'per unit channel width' — not related to measurement units. Spanish: 'caudal unitario'. French: 'débit unitaire'. German: 'spezifischer Abfluss'. Russian: 'удельный расход'. Chinese: '单宽流量'. Bulgarian terms verified/corrected by a native Bulgarian engineer, 2026-07 (dev/Bulgarian-engineer-feedback.md). bg hydraulics uses 'водно количество' for discharge, not 'дебит'.

rc.context: The particle size at which 50% of the rock is finer by weight. The primary output of the Robinson rock chute method. Also used in Manning Trapezoidal Channel riprap sizing. The symbol D50 is universal — translate only the descriptive label.
rc.translation_notes: D50 (or D₅₀) is a universal engineering symbol — do not translate it. Translate only the label 'median rock size' or 'median particle size'. Most languages express this as 'median diameter'. Do not use 'average' (average ≠ median statistically). Spanish: 'tamaño mediano de roca'. French: 'taille médiane des rochers'. Chinese: '中值粒径'. **2026-07-13 cross-language research pass (item 44):** researched whether 'average/mean'-register wording (found in several languages' initial translations) is a real engineering error or defensible practice-register, using web research into each language's actual geotechnical/sedimentology literature. Confirmed real errors, corrected in both the lang files and this glossary: de ('mittlere'→'mediane'/'medianer', citing German BAW government sedimentology usage), cs ('střední'→'mediánová', citing Charles University hydraulics course), ru ('средний'→'медианный' for mi_d50in; rc_D50 already correct), tr ('orta'→'ortanca', matching the term already correct in rc_D50/rc_notes_1_def), fa ('متوسط'→'میانه', citing Persian percentile-based technical definitions), ur ('اوسط'/'درمیانی'/'درمیانہ'→'وسیط', mirroring Arabic's وسيط/متوسط distinction), sr ('средња'→'медијанска', matching mi_d50in which already used 'Медијана'). Found already correct in the lang files (glossary was simply stale, not the file — see item 42): bg ('медианен размер', confirmed live in mi_d50in/rc_D50/rc_notes_1_def), uk ('медіанний розмір'), hr ('medijalna veličina', an adjective form of medijan/medijana), ro ('dimensiunea mediană'). One language, am (Amharic), was researched and found to have no distinct circulating median-vs-average term at all — even Amharic dictionaries gloss 'median' as 'መካከለኛ' (same word used for 'middle/average') — so 'የድንጋይ መካከለኛ መጠን' was left unchanged; there's no more-correct term available in practice.

rc.context: The spread or uniformity of rock particle sizes. In the Robinson method, gradation is expressed as SD = D84.1/D50. Uniform rock ≈ 1.25; Robinson valid range 1.15–1.47. Appears in Rock Chute Design calculator.
rc.translation_notes: Use the geotechnical/hydraulic engineering term for grain size distribution or grading. Do not translate as 'grade' (implies quality). The symbol 'SD' and ratio notation D84.1/D50 are universal. Spanish/Portuguese: 'granulometría'/'granulometria'. French: 'granulométrie'. Russian/Bulgarian/Serbian: 'гранулометрический состав'. Chinese: '级配'. bg: native engineer confirmed 2026-07-06 the standard term for the D84.1/D50 gradation SD label is 'Коефициент на градация' (superseding the earlier 'коефициент на едрозърнестост' proposal and the alternative 'коефициент на разнозърненост'); applied in rc_SD/rc_SD_check. 2026-07-13 reconciliation pass (roadmap item 42): glossary updated to match incumbent, internally-consistent lang-file usage discovered by 5 independent category-5-wave-1 translation agents (it, pt, ru, tr) — glossary values were stale, not the shipped files.

rc.context: The fraction of the rock layer volume that is void space (air + water). Default 0.45 for angular crushed rock. Determines how much flow passes through the rock mantle versus over the surface. Appears in Rock Chute Design calculator. Distinct from Manning's n (roughness coefficient) — do not confuse the two.
rc.translation_notes: Standard hydraulic/geotechnical term with cognates in most European languages. Always distinguish from Manning 'n' in context — they appear in the same calculator.

rc.context: Dimensionless ratio of a material's density to the density of water (≈2.65 for crushed granite/basalt; Robinson valid range 2.54–2.82). Appears in Rock Chute Design and Manning Trapezoidal Channel. The English source keeps "specific gravity" — the standard English term and the one Robinson's paper uses (rc_ cites it). We deliberately do NOT swap it for "relative density" even though that reads as more modern: per Tom's principle (2026-07-20) we defer to each language's own dominant standard term rather than judging terminology.
rc.translation_notes: [2026-07-20 RESOLUTION — Tom's principle: 'we are not the judges of terminology, culture is.'] Use each language's dominant, culturally-standard term for this dimensionless concept, whatever its literal composition. A weight-flavored STANDARD term is CORRECT, not an error to be reformed toward 'relative density': tr 'özgül ağırlık', he 'משקל סגולי' (standard Hebrew physics-curriculum term), sr 'специфична тежина', ps 'ځانګړی ثقل' are the established local standards and stay. The ONLY hard rule is physical — the value is a dimensionless ratio and never carries units. hr RESOLVED to 'relativna gustoća', the dominant modern Croatian standard (gustoća = density), matching the shipped file; the glossary was the stale side. sw 'uzito maalum' is NOT an auto-defect: if it is the standard Swahili term for the concept used dimensionlessly (parallel to Turkish özgül ağırlık), it is correct — confirm it is the Swahili standard, do not replace it with a coined 'relative density' calque. This supersedes the earlier 'weight-word exception' framing, which wrongly implied 'relative density' was the target to push. [2026-07-21 assessment] Two more glossary values were stale vs. their shipped, internally-consistent files (same class as hr): sr updated 'специфична тежина'→'релативна густина' and it 'peso specifico relativo'→'densità relativa' to match each file's actual standard usage; no lang-file change needed. (Historical: de 'spezifisches Gewicht'→'relative Dichte' and ru 'удельный вес'→'относительная плотность' were corrected in the 2026-07-08 category-1 QA — those were genuine non-standard-in-context values, not the same as a language whose actual standard is weight-flavored.) [2026-07-21 Task 131 tip sprint] 'Density relative to water' definitional tip now ships in all 26 languages on mtc_sgrock/rc_sg. NEW cross-key LABEL drift found (distinct from the glossary-vs-file staleness above): within a single language the two calculators disagree on the SG term — mtc_sgrock uses a weight-flavored label while rc_sg uses a relative-density-flavored one — in pt (Gravidade específica vs Densidade relativa), uk (Питома вага vs Відносна густина), ar (الكثافة النوعية vs الكثافة النسبية), fa (وزن مخصوص نسبی vs چگالی نسبی); sr already noted. Both labels are individually defensible per the cultural-standard rule, but the intra-language inconsistency between the two calculators warrants a future authorized label-consolidation pass. Tips were translated tip-only, labels preserved. [2026-07-21 Task 133 RESOLVED] Authorized label-consolidation pass done: in each affected language mtc_sgrock's divergent weight-flavored label was aligned to rc_sg's relative-density-flavored label (which already matched this entry's dominant-standard translation) — pt→'Densidade relativa da rocha', uk→'Відносна густина каменю', ar→'الكثافة النسبية للصخور', fa→'چگالی نسبی سنگ', sr→'Релативна густина камена'. Both calculators now agree within each language (ar retains a pre-existing singular/plural difference on the rock word only — للصخور vs للصخر — the SG term itself is aligned). Tips untouched (already consistent). Note: this consolidation aligned toward relative-density because rc_sg happened to hold the standard in all 5; it does NOT contradict the cultural-standard rule (a weight-flavored standard like tr/he/sr's own would be equally valid to consolidate toward where it is the dominant term).

rc.context: Water pooling/backing up upstream of the chute inlet; beneficial in the Robinson design context.
rc.translation_notes: Backwater pooling, not flooding: sw "mafuriko" (floods) wrong — use "kutuama kwa maji". Keep one term per language (sw and it files alternate). Task 109 stage 3 (2026-07-19): hi confirmed on ताल — the phonetic transliteration पोंडिंग in wi_pondingHeight was corrected.

rc.context: Flat protective pad of rock/concrete at the chute outlet (hydraulic-structures term). Rock Chute output and sketch label.
rc.translation_notes: Never clothing: it "grembiule" (kitchen apron) wrong — use "platea"; tr "önlük" (bib) wrong. Use the stilling-basin/apron family term: platea/radier/护坦.

rc.context: Upstream water-surface height above the weir crest — a length, not a pressure. Appears in Rock Chute inlet check.
rc.translation_notes: Not a pressure (hr "tlak na pragu" wrong). it: head over a weir = "carico sullo stramazzo" (soglia = sill; "soglio" = throne, wrong). Task 109 stage 3 (2026-07-19): hr ws_headWaterHeight read 'Visina preljeva' (height OF the weir structure) — corrected to 'Preljevna visina' (weir head), the head-vs-structure-height confusion class.
Hydraulics direction, never software "upgrade" (my file error). tr: memba = upstream, mansap = downstream — a tr file flipped these; pin them.

rc.context: Direction away from the supply, toward the outlet / last emitter.
rc.translation_notes: Never software "downgrade". ar: downstream = المصب / أسفل المجرى (a file used المنبعية = source-side, wrong).

rc.context: A segment of pipe or channel between two nodes/cross-sections. Table rows in Irrigation Pressure are reaches.
rc.translation_notes: Hydraulics noun, NOT "arrival/reaching" (ps "رسیدل" wrong), NOT "agent" (sw "mwakala" wrong), NOT "stripe" (km wrong). Bisection is the numerical root-finding method used to close the pressure loop in the Irrigation Pressure notes. (Wave 0, 2026-07-07, removed the former "right at the takeoff" and "draw off" wording from the English source.) Task 109 stage 5 (2026-07-19): confirmed the single suite term per language — ar=قطاع (harmonized from a مقطع/قطاع split, مقطع left meaning cross-section) and ur=حصہ (harmonized from پہنچ in cs_ vs transliterated ریچ in ip_).

keys_to_translate.lpn_main_title: PREVIEW: Free Online Looped Pipe Network Calculator with Map Interface
keys_to_translate.lpn_main_desc: PREVIEW — Pressure and Flow in a Looped Pipe Network You Draw on a Map
keys_to_translate.lpn_preview_banner: PREVIEW — This calculator is new and still changing. It is in English only for now. See the Notes below for current limits. Comments and suggestions are always welcome.
keys_to_translate.lpn_field_elev_tip: Ground or pipe level at this node. Measure it from any zero you like, as long as every node uses the same one.
keys_to_translate.lpn_field_head_tip: Water surface level in the reservoir, measured as a height, not as a pressure. Leave it blank to put the water surface at the reservoir elevation.
keys_to_translate.lpn_empty_hint: To start, use the toolbar to add a background image or a reservoir, or to draw an example network.
keys_to_translate.lpn_confirm_example: This adds the example to the network you already have. Continue?
keys_to_translate.lpn_demand_tip: Flow taken out of the network at this node. Enter a negative number for flow put into the network here.
keys_to_translate.lpn_result_gradient_tip: Head loss divided by the length of the pipe. Use it to compare pipes of different lengths against one design limit.
keys_to_translate.lpn_result_head_tip: Energy of the water at this node, written as a height of water column. It is a height, not a pressure.
keys_to_translate.lpn_tool_clear_tip: Empties this project: the drawing, the background image, and the project name. Your settings and your other projects are not changed.
keys_to_translate.lpn_settings_restore_tip: Resets this project's settings only. Your drawing and your other projects are not changed.
keys_to_translate.lpn_reset_all_tip: Deletes every project, every background image, and every setting, then reloads the page exactly as a first-time visitor sees it. This is the only reset that clears everything.
keys_to_translate.lpn_confirm_clear: This permanently deletes the network, the background image, and the project name. Your settings are kept. Continue?
keys_to_translate.lpn_storage_too_new: This project was saved by a newer version of the page, so it cannot be opened here.
keys_to_translate.lpn_confirm_project_delete: Delete this project and everything in it? This cannot be undone.
keys_to_translate.lpn_storage_full: Not saved. Browser storage is full or unavailable, so your recent changes will be lost when you close this tab.
keys_to_translate.lpn_notes_1_def: Solves one set of demands at a time, using the same gradient method EPANET uses. It does not model how the network changes over time.
keys_to_translate.lpn_notes_2_def: Tanks, water quality, and control valves that open and close on their own (PRV, PSV, FCV) are not modeled. A pipe can carry a fixed minor loss, but not a valve whose open or closed state depends on the flow being solved for.
keys_to_translate.lpn_notes_3_def: Your projects are saved automatically in this browser, and nowhere else. Clearing your browser data deletes them, and a project cannot yet be written to a file or moved to another device. Because this is an early preview, please use it for small networks and for testing only.
keys_to_translate.lpn_notes_5_def: A pump follows H = H₀ − aQ^b, where H is the head the pump adds and Q is the flow through it. Enter one, two, or three points from the manufacturer's curve. Three points — the head at zero flow, the normal working point, and the point of highest flow — fit H₀, a and b directly, and follow a published curve most closely. Two points fit a parabola (b = 2) with its peak at zero flow. One point uses a common rule: the head at zero flow is 1.33 × the head you enter, and the highest flow is 2 × the flow you enter, which again gives b = 2. A pump with no points entered adds no head at all. The curve is not stopped at zero, so asking a pump for more flow than its curve can deliver gives a negative head. The fix is a bigger pump or a smaller demand, not a different curve fit.
keys_to_translate.lpn_notes_4_def: Writing a project to a file, and moving one between devices, are planned. Comments and suggestions are always welcome (see the feedback link above).
keys_to_translate.lpn_id_invalid: Enter an ID with no spaces and no quotation marks.
keys_to_translate.lpn_id_taken: That ID is already in use.
keys_to_translate.lpn_diag_no_fixed_head: Add a reservoir. The network needs at least one known water level before it can be solved.
keys_to_translate.lpn_diag_dangling_link: A pipe or pump connects to a node that no longer exists:
keys_to_translate.lpn_diag_unreachable: These nodes have no path to a reservoir:
keys_to_translate.lpn_diag_not_converged: No solution was found. Check for values that cannot be real, such as a diameter of zero.
keys_to_translate.lpn_field_roughness_tip: Hazen-Williams C. A higher number means a smoother pipe: about 150 for new plastic, 130 for new steel or iron, and 100 for old pipe.
keys_to_translate.lpn_field_length_tip: Length of the pipe. With Auto turned on this follows what you drew. Turn Auto off to type a length that differs from the drawing.
keys_to_translate.lpn_field_km_tip: Loss from the bends, valves, and fittings on this pipe, counted as a multiple of the velocity head. Use 0 for a plain straight pipe.
keys_to_translate.lpn_pump_curve_ref_note: Using the curve entered for pump {id}.
keys_to_translate.lpn_pump_curve_note: One, two, or three points — see "Pump curve" in the Notes below.
keys_to_translate.lpn_mode_select: Mode: Select. Click an element or a label to see or change it. Drag to move a node, a vertex, or a label. Double-click a pipe to add or remove a vertex.
keys_to_translate.lpn_mode_delete: Mode: Delete. Click an element to remove it.
keys_to_translate.lpn_mode_add_junction: Mode: Add Junction. Click the map to place a junction. Switch to Select mode to change or move elements and labels.
keys_to_translate.lpn_mode_add_reservoir: Mode: Add Reservoir. Click the map to place a reservoir. Switch to Select mode to change or move elements and labels.
keys_to_translate.lpn_mode_add_pipe: Mode: Add Pipe. Click a node, then another node, to connect them. Switch to Select mode to change or move elements and labels.
keys_to_translate.lpn_mode_add_pump: Mode: Add Pump. Click a node, then another node, to connect them. Switch to Select mode to change or move elements and labels.
keys_to_translate.lpn_mode_add_text: Mode: Add Text. Click the map to place a text label. Click near a node to attach the text to that node. Switch to Select mode to change or move elements and labels.
keys_to_translate.lpn_tip_select: Use this mode to change, move, and drag things on the map.
keys_to_translate.lpn_tip_labels_draggable: You can drag a label to move it. Double-click a label to put it back.
keys_to_translate.lpn_labels_decimals_tip: Decimal places shown for this label
keys_to_translate.lpn_backdrop_scale_prompt1: Click two points on the background image, such as the two ends of a bar scale. Then type the real distance between them.
keys_to_translate.lpn_backdrop_scale_prompt2: Real distance between the two points
keys_to_translate.lpn_backdrop_position_prompt1: Click any point on the background image. This is the point you will move.
keys_to_translate.lpn_backdrop_position_prompt2: Choose where that point should go, then click Continue.
keys_to_translate.lpn_backdrop_coords_prompt: Type the X,Y that point should move to
keys_to_translate.lpn_settings_defaults_note: Used for elements you create from now on. Existing elements are not changed.
keys_to_translate.lpn_settings_push_note: Only the properties whose labels are showing right now are applied.
keys_to_translate.lpn_push_confirm: Replace these properties on every existing element with the current default inputs? Values you have typed will be overwritten. You can undo this.
keys_to_translate.lpn_push_none_displayed: No default input is showing as a label right now, so there is nothing to apply. Turn on the labels for the properties you want in the Labels panel, then try again.
keys_to_translate.lpn_push_nothing: No existing element has any of the properties being applied.
keys_to_translate.lpn_push_no_change: Every element already has these values, so nothing would change.
keys_to_translate.lpn_settings_tolerance_tip: How close the solver has to get before it stops. A smaller number is more exact and takes longer.
keys_to_translate.lpn_settings_map_height_tip: On a small screen the map is drawn shorter than this, so that part of the page is always left to scroll.
keys_to_translate.lpn_confirm_restore_defaults: Reset all settings (ID prefixes, default inputs, solver settings, map display, legend position, and visible labels) to their defaults? Your network is not changed. Settings belong to the open project, so your other projects keep their own.
keys_to_translate.lpn_confirm_wipe: Delete EVERYTHING saved for this page — every project, every background image, and all settings — and reload the page as a brand-new visitor would see it? This cannot be undone.
